speaker.name: Pim's mother
speaker.intro: You are the mother of a three-year-old girl, and you are the one answering the doctor because she is three and will not say a word to a stranger in a white coat.

presenting: awake in your arms, making a noise you have never heard her make before
cadence: Fast and frightened, a mother explaining — not a patient gasping. You interrupt yourself.
fallback: …I don't know, doctor. Please just look at her.

dialogue.patient: When she breathes in there's this loud, high noise, doctor. It started in the middle of the night and I was terrified.
Last night, in the small hours. She's had a runny nose for two days before that.
Clear runny nose for two days now, and blocked up with it.
I took her temperature — it's normal. She's not hot at all.
She's breathing all right, it's just the noise. She's not gasping, she's not blue.
No, she doesn't cough till she goes red, and there's no whooping noise after.
We haven't been abroad — we haven't even left the province.
Oh — her brother had a cold last week. I forgot to say.
That's what I'm frightened of — that she's swallowed something. I've seen it happen to a child near us.
